item.title: Amish Christmas Cookie Tour in Lancaster — Fri Nov 20 — Amish Farm and House
item.description: Interact with Amish families in their homes and learn about their heritage while sampling homemade cookies. This holiday season, make new friends, learn new recipes, and create memories to last a lifetime. Take a step away from the stress of the holidays, slow down, and let us take you on a relaxing and festive journey. We will visit three authentic Amish homes to sample homemade Christmas cookies. You’ll leave with an appreciation of another culture, along with recipes and cookies to take home and enjoy. Dad doesn’t need another tie, and Mom doesn’t want another gift card. Spend time with your loved ones this holiday season; join us for our Christmas cookie tour! IMPORTANT: Please indicate at the time of booking if you are traveling with another party, so that we can do our best to ensure you travel together. Our buses hold a maximum of 14 passengers. item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Nov 24, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Feeling Lucky: Mistletoe Season — Wed Dec 2, 6:30 PM — Lucky Dog Cafe
item.description: A neighborhood cafe on Columbia Avenue, the kind of easygoing local spot where there’s no dress code and no scene, just a comfortable room where people actually talk. December fills up with parties full of people you already know. This is the other kind of night: a room full of singles who showed up on purpose, a game at your table so nobody starts cold, and a Wednesday that actually goes somewhere. How the night works: You check in with a host and get a name tag. There’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements. First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play. That’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold, and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. Then the structure drops away and it’s open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it’s working. By that point you’ve already met most of the room. Last, one-on-one

item.description:

Get ready to buzz into the holiday season with a fun, hands-on coding challenge! Join us at the library for a festive STEM workshop using Bee-Bot programmable floor robots.Kids will pick a holiday mission card and program their Bee-Bot to navigate a custom Christmas mat, collecting the right presents and delivering them to the matching-colored Christmas tree. item.title: Make & Take: Christmas Coffee Cozie — Sat Dec 19 — Bird-in-Hand Artisan Village
item.description: Learn to crochet colorful holiday gifts Try your hand at crochet and go home with a cute Christmas coffee cozie set suitable for gifting. In this-two-hour workshop for beginners, local artist Paula Hughes of Soft and Simple Designs will guide you through the process of selecting yarn, crocheting a cozie for a coffee cup and packaging it in a gift bag along with a packet of hot chocolate. You can also attach a small crocheted wreath to the cozie, or use the wreath as an ornament to decorate a tree or trim a gift package. Paula Hughes will show you basic crochet stitches and answer your questions about this relaxing art of turning soft yarns into useful and decorative items. This Make & Take is also appropriate for kids ages 10 and up. Reserve your space today! $22 per person includes instruction and all supplies for a ready-to-give handmade gift (red or green yarn for cozie, disposable cup, wreath kit, decorative button, hot chocolate, gift bag). item.title: ExtraGive: What Do You Love About Lancaster’s History? — Fri Nov 20, 5:00 PM — The Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy
item.description:
What do you love about Lancaster’s history? The people? The places? The stories that shaped our community? This ExtraGive, LancasterHistory is celebrating it all, and they want you to be part of the fun!
Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History & Democracy! Drop in downtown between 5–8 PM for a special evening of Pay-What-You-Can admission at the Stevens & Smith Center! Explore their newest museum, discover a pop-up display featuring fascinating pieces of Lancaster’s history (some familiar favorites and others that might surprise you), and enjoy a special flash talk at 5:30 PM with Stephanie Townrow, LancasterHistory’s Director of Interpretation & Exhibitions.
Throughout the evening, hear from familiar community voices in a rotating video sharing what they love most about Lancaster’s history, and add your own through a fun, interactive display.
